ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.mutualInfo.statement: For a kernel $\kappa$ from $T$ into a product space $S\times U$ and a measure $\mu$ on $T$, $I_k[\kappa,\mu]$ denotes the mutual information of the kernel $\kappa$ with respect to $\mu$.

ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.mutualInfo_nonn.statement: Let $\kappa$ be a kernel from $T$ into $S \times U$ that has almost everywhere finite kernel support with respect to the measure $\mu$. Then $0 \le I_k[\kappa,\mu]$.
ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.mutualInfo_nonn.sketch: Replace $\kappa$ by an almost-everywhere equal kernel with finite kernel support (`AEFiniteKernelSupport.mk`), which does not change the mutual information; for such a kernel the mutual information is an average of measure mutual informations, each nonnegative by `measureMutualInfo_nonneg`.
